      "title": "Duplicate `downsize` method overrides the 4-argument API",
      "body": "There are two definitions of `OptimizedImage.downsize` in this file (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` API no longer exists. Any existing caller passing two numeric dimensions will now invoke the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` method: the third argument is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the fourth as an options hash, causing `TypeError` (`Numeric#[]`) or an invalid `-resize` command. The old method should be removed or renamed, and all callers updated."
    },

      "body": "`maxSizeKB` is hard-coded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to both images and attachments. If the site has a lower `max_attachment_size_kb`, users can now upload attachments up to 10MB from the browser, and the server-side change in this PR does not downsize non-image attachments. This bypasses configured upload limits and may allow abuse or disk exhaustion."
    },
    {

      "line": 55,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "API URL download limit hard-coded to 10MB for all file types",
      "body": "The API URL upload path now downloads up to `10.megabytes` for every file type, instead of respecting `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` or an attachment size limit. The new downsize loop only applies to images, so a non-image URL up to 10MB is passed to `Upload.create_for` even when the site's max attachment size is lower. This bypasses the configured server-side upload limit."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Downsize failure is ignored and oversized images may still be saved",
      "body": "`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (see `convert_with`), but this loop ignores the return value and simply retries. After five failed attempts it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized file. If image processing is unavailable or repeatedly fails, an oversized image is stored, defeating the site's `max_image_size_kb` limit."
    },

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` method overrides the 4-argument API
findings.body: There are two definitions of `OptimizedImage.downsize` in this file (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` API no longer exists. Any existing caller passing two numeric dimensions will now invoke the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` method: the third argument is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the fourth as an options hash, causing `TypeError` (`Numeric#[]`) or an invalid `-resize` command. The old method should be removed or renamed, and all callers updated.

findings.title: Client-side upload size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all types
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` is hard-coded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to both images and attachments. If the site has a lower `max_attachment_size_kb`, users can now upload attachments up to 10MB from the browser, and the server-side change in this PR does not downsize non-image attachments. This bypasses configured upload limits and may allow abuse or disk exhaustion.

findings.title: API URL download limit hard-coded to 10MB for all file types
findings.body: The API URL upload path now downloads up to `10.megabytes` for every file type, instead of respecting `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` or an attachment size limit. The new downsize loop only applies to images, so a non-image URL up to 10MB is passed to `Upload.create_for` even when the site's max attachment size is lower. This bypasses the configured server-side upload limit.

findings.title: Downsize failure is ignored and oversized images may still be saved
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (see `convert_with`), but this loop ignores the return value and simply retries. After five failed attempts it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized file. If image processing is unavailable or repeatedly fails, an oversized image is stored, defeating the site's `max_image_size_kb` limit.

findings.title: 413 error message shows hard-coded 10MB limit
findings.body: The 413 error path now displays a hard-coded 10 MB limit regardless of the site's actual `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`, so the user may see an incorrect accepted size. Use the configured value or a generic message.

findings.title: No tests added for automatic downsize behavior
findings.body: No tests were added for the new automatic downsize behavior, particularly failure paths where `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`, or for the duplicate `downsize` method in `OptimizedImage`. Without coverage, these regressions are likely to go unnoticed.
